messages:
acme-dev-sre: Hey, private deployment failing after we enabled the VPC connector. App calls to Redwood API and pip installs time out. Getting TLS handshake / cert errors for some hosts. Pls help. Repro steps below.

sara-support: Sorry about that — can you share the failing curl/pip logs and your egress allowlist? We'll triage.

acme-dev-sre: here's a minimal repro:
```
curl -v https://model-registry.prod.redwood.ai/v1/models
* About to connect() to model-registry.prod.redwood.ai port 443 (#0)
* Connected to proxy.example.corp (10.0.0.1) port 3128
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* SSL certificate problem: certificate is not yet valid
``` 
Also pip install fails resolving pypi: timeout.

josh-deploy: Thanks. This is usually an egress block or TLS intercept issue. Can you confirm if your perimeter proxy is doing TLS inspection or SNI-filtering? Also we need these FQDNs opened outbound (TCP 443 unless noted):
- model-registry.prod.redwood.ai
- models.prod.redwood.ai
- auth.prod.redwood.ai
- telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai
- storage.prod.redwood.ai (model blobs)
- packages.ubuntu.com
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- registry-1.docker.io
- ghcr.io
Do not allowlist IPs if you have a CDN — use FQDN/SNI pass-through. If you must IP allowlist, ping the FQDN and share the returned IPs but expect them to change.

sam-cs: Also need outbound DNS resolution (UDP 53 or DoT 853) or allow egress to your recursive resolver. OCSP/CRL checks happen on 443; make sure TLS inspection isn't substituting certs.

mei-eng-ml: For model downloads we use HTTP2/ALPN h2 and long TLS sessions + range requests. Ensure ALPN h2 is allowed and your proxy forwards HTTP2 if possible. If you see `SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` it's TLS interception.

acme-dev-sre: We opened the FQDNs but still see `SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired` when curl'ing telemetry. Proxy team says they're doing TLS interception for malware scanning.

sara-support: If TLS interception is happening you need TLS bypass for the Redwood FQDNs. Bypass rules should match exact hostnames with SNI passthrough. Example curl test from a host in your VPC (no proxy):
```
curl -vk https://telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai/health
* Connected to telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai (54.23.12.34) port 443
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate verified
> GET /health HTTP/2
< 200 OK
```
If that succeeds but your proxied request fails it's the interceptor.

josh-deploy: One more note — for package installs allow: packages.ubuntu.com and the mirror network; for pip allow pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org. For docker pulls allow registry-1.docker.io and ghcr.io and permit TCP 443 to those hosts. If you use STS/KMS for private deployments also allow sts.amazonaws.com and your KMS endpoints.

acme-dev-sre: ok added TLS bypass entries for the redwood hostnames and allowed pypi/ubuntu. Tests pass now. Thanks! :tada:

deploy-bot: Closed issue #7432 — follow-up if regressions seen.

sara-support: Great — marking as resolved. If anything else crop up please reopen or DM.
